families.name: Template expressions
families.introduction: Reported while a template's expressions and directives are parsed, before any types are checked.

families.name: Template analysis
families.introduction: Reported while templates are type-checked against their Go code, and while components, props, assets and styles are linked.

families.name: Rendering
families.introduction: Reported by generated code while a page renders. They appear in the server log rather than in build output, and the page still renders: a nil read or an out-of-range index gives a zero value instead of a panic.

codes.name: InvalidNumberLiteral
codes.title: Invalid number literal
codes.summary: A number in a template expression is malformed.
codes.detail: The expression parser could not read a numeric literal, for example because it has two decimal points or a stray letter.
codes.fix: Write the number as a plain integer or decimal, such as 42 or 3.5.

codes.name: InvalidStringLiteral
codes.title: Invalid string literal
codes.summary: A quoted string in a template expression is malformed.
codes.detail: The parser could not read a string literal, usually because of an unterminated quote or an invalid escape. It is also reported when an object literal's key is neither an identifier nor a valid string.
codes.fix: Close the string with the same quote it opened with, and escape any quote inside it.

codes.name: InvalidEscapeSequence
codes.title: Invalid escape sequence
codes.summary: A rune literal contains an escape sequence that is not valid.
codes.detail: Rune literals such as r'\n' accept the usual Go escapes. Anything else after the backslash is rejected.
codes.fix: Use a valid escape, such as \n, \t, \\ or \', or write the character directly.

codes.name: InvalidTemporalFormat
codes.title: Invalid date, time or duration
codes.summary: A date, time, datetime or duration literal does not match its expected format.
codes.detail: Temporal literals are parsed when the template is built. A datetime must be RFC 3339 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ), dates and times have their own fixed formats, and durations use Go's duration syntax, such as 1h30m.
codes.fix: Rewrite the value in the format the message names.

codes.name: InvalidRuneLiteral
codes.title: Invalid rune literal
codes.summary: A rune literal does not contain exactly one character.
codes.detail: A rune literal, written r'x', holds a single character or a single escape sequence. An empty literal or one with several characters is rejected.
codes.fix: Put exactly one character between the quotes, or use a string if you need more.

codes.name: InvalidTemplateLiteral
codes.title: Invalid template literal
codes.summary: A template literal is not enclosed in backticks.
codes.detail: Template literals, which interpolate values with ${...}, must start and end with a backtick.
codes.fix: Enclose the literal in backticks.

codes.name: UnterminatedInterpolation
codes.title: Unterminated interpolation
codes.summary: An interpolation is opened but never closed.
codes.detail: Text interpolation {{ ... }} needs a closing }}, and a ${...} inside a template literal needs a closing }. The parser reached the end of the text first.
codes.fix: Add the missing closing braces.

codes.name: UnexpectedToken
codes.title: Unexpected token
codes.summary: The parser found a token where it expected a value or a different token.
codes.detail: This is reported when an expression has an operator or punctuation in a position where a value belongs. It is also reported for composite type arguments such as []T, which template expressions do not support.
codes.fix: Check the expression around the highlighted token. For composite type arguments, declare a named type in the script block and use that instead.

codes.name: UnexpectedEOF
codes.title: Unexpected end of expression
codes.summary: The expression ended before it was complete.
codes.detail: The parser was still expecting a value, for example after an operator or an opening bracket, when the expression ran out.
codes.fix: Finish the expression, or remove the trailing operator.

codes.name: MissingIdentifier
codes.title: Missing identifier
codes.summary: An identifier is missing after '.', '?.' or '@'.
codes.detail: Member access and optional chaining need a field or method name after the dot, and the @ prefix needs a name after it.
codes.fix: Add the missing name, or remove the dangling dot.

codes.name: MissingOperand
codes.title: Missing operand
codes.summary: An operator has nothing to operate on.
codes.detail: A binary operator needs a value on its right, a unary operator needs a value after it, a p-for loop needs a collection after 'in', and an object key needs a value.
codes.fix: Add the missing value.

codes.name: MissingClosingDelimiter
codes.title: Missing closing bracket
codes.summary: A ']', ')' or '}' is missing.
codes.detail: An index expression, parenthesised expression, array literal or object literal was opened but not closed before something else appeared.
codes.fix: Add the closing bracket the message names.

codes.name: MissingSeparator
codes.title: Missing separator
codes.summary: A ',' or ':' is missing between parts of an expression.
codes.detail: Object literals need ':' between key and value and ',' between entries, function calls need ',' between arguments, and a ternary needs ':' between its two outcomes.
codes.fix: Add the separator the message names.

codes.name: IncompleteConstruct
codes.title: Incomplete expression
codes.summary: An index, function call, type argument list or ternary is not fully written.
codes.detail: Examples are an empty index such as items[], a call with a trailing comma such as f(a,), or a ternary with no value after '?' or ':'.
codes.fix: Complete the construct, or remove the stray separator.

codes.name: ExpressionDepthExceeded
codes.title: Expression nested too deeply
codes.summary: An expression is nested more deeply than the parser allows.
codes.detail: The parser limits nesting so that malformed or hostile templates cannot exhaust the stack. Real templates stay far below the limit.
codes.fix: Move the logic into a function in the script block and call it from the template.

codes.name: DisallowedFeature
codes.title: Feature not allowed here
codes.summary: The expression uses a feature this context does not allow.
codes.detail: Some places accept only a restricted kind of expression. For example, dynamic index access is not allowed where the value must be known when the template is built.
codes.fix: Use a simpler expression here, or compute the value in the script block.

codes.name: LexerError
codes.title: Unreadable expression
codes.summary: The expression contains characters the lexer cannot read.
codes.detail: The lexer turns an expression into tokens before it is parsed. This is reported when it meets a character or sequence that is not part of the expression language.
codes.fix: Remove or quote the character the message points at.

codes.name: TrailingTokens
codes.title: Unexpected text after expression
codes.summary: Tokens remain after a complete expression.
codes.detail: The parser read a whole expression but more text follows it, for example two values with no operator between them.
codes.fix: Join the parts with an operator, or remove the extra text.

example.message: Invalid syntax. A comma is not a valid operator here. If you are trying to write a for-loop, variables must be enclosed in parentheses, e.g., `(index, item) in collection`.

codes.name: UnexpectedComma
codes.title: Unexpected comma
codes.summary: A comma is used where it is not an operator.
codes.detail: Commas only separate arguments, array items and object entries. The usual cause is a p-for loop with two variables written without parentheses.
codes.fix: Enclose loop variables in parentheses, such as (index, item) in collection.

codes.name: ConflictingDirectives
codes.title: Conflicting directives
codes.summary: An element has two directives that cannot be combined.
codes.detail: p-text and p-html both replace an element's content, so only one can apply. p-else and p-else-if both close a conditional chain, so an element can carry only one.
codes.fix: Remove one of the two directives.

codes.name: DuplicateDirective
codes.title: Duplicate directive
codes.summary: The same directive appears more than once on an element.
codes.detail: Only one instance of a directive, or of a p-bind for the same attribute, takes effect. The message gives the position of the first.
codes.fix: Remove the duplicate, or merge the two expressions.

codes.name: InvalidDirectiveValue
codes.title: Invalid directive value
codes.summary: A directive's value is empty or not valid.
codes.detail: p-ref needs a name that is a valid JavaScript identifier, and p-slot needs a slot name.
codes.fix: Give the directive a valid value.

codes.name: InvalidDirectivePlacement
codes.title: p-else without p-if
codes.summary: A p-else or p-else-if does not follow an element with p-if or p-else-if.
codes.detail: A conditional chain must be made of sibling elements in order. Whitespace and comments between them are ignored, but any other node breaks the chain.
codes.fix: Move the element directly after its p-if, or remove what separates them.

codes.name: DirectivePrecedence
codes.title: Directive written before p-for
codes.summary: A directive is written before p-for, but p-for is evaluated first.
codes.detail: p-for always has the highest precedence, so another directive written before it still runs once per item. The order in the source suggests otherwise.
codes.fix: Write p-for before the element's other directives and dynamic attributes.

codes.name: InvalidDirectiveTarget
codes.title: Directive not supported on this element
codes.summary: A directive is used on an element that does not support it.
codes.detail: p-model binds a form value, so it only works on <input>, <textarea> and <select>.
codes.fix: Move the directive to a supported element.

example.message: Elements with 'p-for' directives should have a unique 'p-key' binding for efficient updates. The framework will fall back to using the loop index, which may cause performance issues or unexpected behaviour with stateful components.

codes.name: MissingLoopKey
codes.title: p-for without p-key
codes.summary: A p-for loop has no p-key.
codes.detail: Without a key, the loop index is used to match items between renders. When items are added, removed or reordered, that can reuse the wrong element and lose its state, and it does more work.
codes.fix: Add a p-key bound to a value that identifies each item, such as its ID.

codes.name: AttributeConflict
codes.title: Static and dynamic attribute conflict
codes.summary: An attribute is set statically and also by a dynamic binding.
codes.detail: The dynamic :attr or p-bind:attr value overwrites the static one, so the static value never shows.
codes.fix: Remove the static attribute, or fold it into the binding's expression.

codes.name: DirectiveOverwritesContent
codes.title: Directive overwrites content
codes.summary: An element has children that p-text or p-html will replace.
codes.detail: p-text and p-html set the element's whole content, so its existing children are discarded at runtime and only mislead readers.
codes.fix: Remove the children, or drop the directive.

codes.name: CSSParseError
codes.title: Invalid CSS selector
codes.summary: A CSS selector could not be parsed.
codes.detail: Selectors used to query the template, for example in tests, are parsed with a CSS selector parser. This is reported when the selector is not valid CSS.
codes.fix: Correct the selector.

codes.name: InternalParserError
codes.title: Internal parser error
codes.summary: The expression parser reached a state it should not. This should not normally happen.
codes.detail: A defensive check in the parser fired. The expression may be unusual, but the parser should have reported a clearer error.
codes.fix: Open an issue on GitHub with the expression that caused it.

codes.name: DuplicateAttribute
codes.title: Duplicate attribute
codes.summary: The same static attribute is written more than once on an element.
codes.detail: HTML keeps the first occurrence and silently discards the rest, so the later value never takes effect.
codes.fix: Remove the duplicate.

example.message: The '_memo' attribute is set statically. Its value never changes, so this element and its children are skipped on every re-render after the first. Use the p-memo directive instead, for example 'p-memo="item"'.

codes.name: StaticMemoAttribute
codes.title: Static _memo attribute
codes.summary: _memo is written as a static attribute instead of the p-memo directive.
codes.detail: A static value never changes, so the memo check always matches and the element and its children stop updating after their first render.
codes.fix: Use the p-memo directive with the value that should trigger a re-render, such as p-memo="item".

example.message: Undefined variable: state.Titl. Did you mean 'state.Title'?

codes.name: UndefinedVariable
codes.title: Undefined variable
codes.summary: A template refers to a name that is not defined.
codes.detail: The name is not a field of state or props, a loop variable, an import, or a built-in. When a defined name is close, the message suggests it. It is also reported when the template calls an unexported function from the script block, which templates cannot see.
codes.fix: Fix the spelling, define the value in the script block, or export the function by capitalising its name.

codes.name: TypeMismatch
codes.title: Type mismatch
codes.summary: A value's type does not match the type expected where it is used.
codes.detail: It is an error when a function argument has the wrong type or a ternary's two outcomes have incompatible types. It is a warning when an array or object literal mixes element types, or when a field is read through a pointer that may be nil, which is then checked at runtime.
codes.fix: Convert the value to the expected type, or make the elements of the literal share one type.

codes.name: CircularDependency
codes.title: Circular dependency
codes.summary: Components, partials or imports depend on each other in a cycle.
codes.detail: A component that renders a partial which, directly or through others, renders the first component again can never finish expanding. The message lists the cycle.
codes.fix: Break the cycle, for example by moving shared markup into a partial that neither side imports back.

codes.name: UnresolvedImport
codes.title: Unresolved import
codes.summary: An import path for a component, partial or Go package could not be resolved.
codes.detail: The import does not name a file in the project or a package the module can find. CSS @import paths that cannot be found are reported as T114.
codes.fix: Check the path against the module name and directory layout, such as myapp/partials/card.pk.

codes.name: DeprecatedElement
codes.title: Email element in a web page
codes.summary: A PikoML <pml-*> element is used outside an email template.
codes.detail: PikoML components are built for HTML email and render table-based layouts. They belong in .pk files under the emails directory.
codes.fix: Use standard HTML elements or Piko components (<piko:*>) in web pages.

codes.name: MissingPartialAttribute
codes.title: Missing is attribute
codes.summary: A <piko:partial> or <piko:element> has no is attribute.
codes.detail: <piko:partial> needs is set to the alias of an imported partial, and <piko:element> needs is set to the tag it should render.
codes.fix: Add the is attribute.

codes.name: InvalidPartialAttribute
codes.title: Invalid is attribute
codes.summary: The is attribute on <piko:partial> or <piko:element> has a value it cannot use.
codes.detail: <piko:partial is> must be a static string, because partials are resolved when the project is built. <piko:element is> cannot target piko:partial, piko:slot or piko:element.
codes.fix: Use a static partial alias, or a plain HTML tag name.

codes.name: UndefinedPartialAlias
codes.title: Undefined partial alias
codes.summary: A <piko:partial is> names an alias that is not imported.
codes.detail: Partials are imported in the Go script block under an alias, and is refers to that alias.
codes.fix: Import the partial under that alias, or fix the alias in is.

codes.name: PartialLoadError
codes.title: Partial could not be loaded
codes.summary: An imported partial's file could not be loaded.
codes.detail: The file may be missing, or it may not contain a <template> block.
codes.fix: Check that the file exists at the imported path and has a <template> block.

codes.name: SlotMismatch
codes.title: No such slot
codes.summary: Content is passed to a slot the component does not have.
codes.detail: The component declares no <piko:slot> with that name, so the content is never rendered. When a declared slot name is close, the message suggests it.
codes.fix: Use one of the component's slot names, or add the slot to the component.

codes.name: VariableShadowing
codes.title: Name shadows a built-in
codes.summary: A function or variable has the same name as a built-in or an import alias.
codes.detail: A user-defined function that shadows a Piko system symbol or global function, or a local variable that shadows an import alias, makes the template call something other than what a reader expects.
codes.fix: Rename the function or variable.

codes.name: ScriptMissingLang
codes.title: Script block has no language
codes.summary: A <script> block has no lang or type attribute.
codes.detail: Piko needs to know whether a script is server-side Go or client-side TypeScript or JavaScript.
codes.fix: Add lang="go" (or type="application/x-go") for Go, lang="ts" for TypeScript, or lang="js" for JavaScript.

codes.name: AssetResolutionError
codes.title: Asset not found
codes.summary: An asset path could not be resolved, or an image's responsive attributes are incomplete.
codes.detail: The path may use a module alias that cannot be expanded or point at a file that does not exist. For responsive images, densities needs width or sizes, and each density must look like x1, x2 or 2x.
codes.fix: Check the path and the file, and complete the responsive attributes the message names.

codes.name: AssetProfileError
codes.title: Asset profile not found
codes.summary: An asset profile named on a tag is missing from the configuration or has no settings.
codes.detail: The tag is still processed, using only its explicit attributes.
codes.fix: Define the profile in the configuration, or remove the reference.

codes.name: CSSImportError
codes.title: CSS import failed
codes.summary: A CSS @import could not be resolved, or imports form a cycle.
codes.detail: Piko inlines @import rules when it builds a component's styles. The imported file must exist and must not import, directly or indirectly, the file that imports it.
codes.fix: Fix the import path, or break the cycle.

codes.name: CSSProcessingError
codes.title: CSS error
codes.summary: The CSS processor reported a problem in a component's styles.
codes.detail: Styles are parsed and minified by esbuild. Its errors, warnings and notes are reported with this code and keep esbuild's severity.
codes.fix: Correct the CSS at the reported position.

codes.name: GoCompilationError
codes.title: Go compilation error
codes.summary: The Go compiler rejected code generated from a component, and the error is mapped back to the .pk file.
codes.detail: Piko compiles each component's script block together with code generated from its template. Errors are reported at the matching place in the .pk source where possible.
codes.fix: Fix the Go code at the reported position, as you would for go build.

codes.name: CollectionError
codes.title: Collection error
codes.summary: The collection system failed while resolving a collection's types.
codes.detail: Templates that use p-collection or the collection functions need the collection service to read the collection's items when the project is built.
codes.fix: Check the collection's configuration and content, and the message for the underlying cause.

codes.name: FatalAnnotationError
codes.title: Analysis failed
codes.summary: A stage of template analysis failed and could not continue.
codes.detail: The build reports what it could and stops processing the affected components. The message names the stage and the underlying error.
codes.fix: Fix the cause in the message. If it looks like a bug, open an issue on GitHub with the component that triggers it.

codes.name: EventPlaceholderMisuse
codes.title: $event or $form misused
codes.summary: $event or $form is used outside an event handler, or used in a way it does not support.
codes.detail: $event and $form only exist inside p-on and p-event handlers, and are passed whole: reading a property from them in the template is not supported. The browser's own event object is $event, not event.
codes.fix: Pass $event or $form whole to the handler, and read their properties inside it.

codes.name: InvalidLoopExpression
codes.title: Invalid p-for expression
codes.summary: A p-for expression is not a valid loop, or loops over a type that cannot be iterated.
codes.detail: p-for takes the form item in items, or (index, item) in items, over a slice, array, map, string or integer.
codes.fix: Write the loop as item in items over an iterable value.

codes.name: LoopVariableShadow
codes.title: Loop variable shadows a built-in
codes.summary: A p-for loop variable has the same name as a built-in symbol or global function.
codes.detail: Inside the loop, the name refers to the loop variable, so the built-in cannot be used there.
codes.fix: Rename the loop variable.

codes.name: ConditionalTypeError
codes.title: Condition is not a boolean
codes.summary: A p-if, p-else-if or p-show expression is not a boolean.
codes.detail: Conditions must be booleans. Piko does not treat strings, numbers or pointers as true or false implicitly.
codes.fix: Compare explicitly, such as len(items) > 0, or use the ~ operator for truthiness, such as ~value.

codes.name: ModelTypeError
codes.title: p-model target is not assignable
codes.summary: A p-model expression is not a variable that can be assigned to.
codes.detail: p-model writes the input's value back, so it needs a field, such as state.Name, not a call or a computed value.
codes.fix: Bind p-model to a field.

codes.name: BindingTypeError
codes.title: Binding has the wrong type
codes.summary: A p-class, :class, p-style, p-key or p-context binding has a type it does not expect.
codes.detail: It is an error when :class is not a string, slice or map. It is a warning when p-class or p-style has another type, when p-key is a struct, map or slice, or when p-context does not resolve to a string.
codes.fix: Give the binding the type the message names.

codes.name: AttributeTypeError
codes.title: Attribute value is not text
codes.summary: A dynamic attribute's value has no defined text form.
codes.detail: Without String or MarshalText, Go's default formatting is used, which is rarely what you want in HTML. It is also reported for p-timeline outside .pkc files, where it is not supported.
codes.fix: Implement fmt.Stringer or encoding.TextMarshaler on the type, convert the value to a string, or use a server. attribute if it is only needed on the server.

codes.name: UnknownProp
codes.title: Unknown prop
codes.summary: A prop is passed to a component that does not define it.
codes.detail: The component's Props struct has no field for the prop, so the value is ignored. When a defined prop is close, the message suggests it.
codes.fix: Use the prop name the component defines, or add the field to its Props struct.

codes.name: MissingRequiredProp
codes.title: Missing required prop
codes.summary: A component is used without a prop it requires.
codes.detail: The prop's field in the component's Props struct is marked required.
codes.fix: Pass the prop, or give it a default in the component.

codes.name: PropTypeMismatch
codes.title: Prop has the wrong type
codes.summary: The value passed to a prop does not match the prop's declared type.
codes.detail: When the value could be converted, the message suggests adding coerce:"true" to the prop's field.
codes.fix: Pass a value of the declared type, or add coerce:"true" to the field so Piko converts it.

codes.name: DuplicatePropBinding
codes.title: Prop bound twice
codes.summary: A prop is given both a standard binding and a server-only binding.
codes.detail: The server-only binding takes precedence, so the standard binding is ignored.
codes.fix: Remove one of the bindings.

codes.name: PropDefaultError
codes.title: Invalid prop default
codes.summary: A prop's default value or default factory does not fit the prop's type.
codes.detail: It is an error when the default is invalid or a factory returns the wrong type. It is a warning when a default written as text cannot be parsed as the prop's type.
codes.fix: Correct the default so it has the prop's type.

codes.name: PropDefinitionError
codes.title: Invalid Props struct
codes.summary: A component's Props struct is malformed.
codes.detail: Two fields map to the same prop name, tags conflict, or an embedded field's props cannot be collected.
codes.fix: Give each prop a unique name and consistent tags.

codes.name: QueryPropError
codes.title: Invalid query prop
codes.summary: A prop bound to a query parameter has an invalid query tag or type.
codes.detail: It is an error when the query tag is empty or the prop is a slice or map, which query binding does not support. It is a warning when the prop is not a string, because query parameters are strings.
codes.fix: Name the parameter in the tag, such as query:"page", and use a string prop or add coerce:"true".

codes.name: HandlerArgumentError
codes.title: Handler arguments do not match
codes.summary: A handler or action call has the wrong number or types of arguments.
codes.detail: The call in the template does not match the exported client function's parameters or the action's input.
codes.fix: Pass the arguments the function or action declares.

codes.name: HandlerExpressionError
codes.title: Invalid event handler
codes.summary: An event handler is not a function call, or uses an unknown or incompatible modifier.
codes.detail: p-on handlers must call a function or method. The supported modifiers are .prevent, .stop, .once, .self, .passive and .capture, and .passive cannot be combined with .prevent.
codes.fix: Write the handler as a call, such as save($event), and use supported modifiers.

codes.name: BuiltinFunctionError
codes.title: Built-in function misused
codes.summary: A built-in function such as len, cap, append, min or max is called incorrectly.
codes.detail: The call has the wrong number of arguments, or arguments of a type the function does not accept, such as len on a number or min with mixed types.
codes.fix: Call the function as Go does.

codes.name: TranslationFunctionError
codes.title: Translation function misused
codes.summary: A translation function such as T, LT or LTC is called incorrectly, or names a missing key.
codes.detail: It is an error when the function has no arguments or an argument is not a string. When the key is missing from a locale's translations, it is reported as info if a fallback is given and as a warning if not.
codes.fix: Pass the key as a string, and add the key to the translations or give a fallback.

codes.name: UndefinedMember
codes.title: No such field or method
codes.summary: A field, method or package member does not exist.
codes.detail: The type, or the package, has no member with that name. When a member is close, the message suggests it, and it points out len() when a property such as .length is used.
codes.fix: Use a member the type defines.

codes.name: InvalidIndexing
codes.title: Invalid index
codes.summary: A value is indexed when it cannot be, or with an index of the wrong type.
codes.detail: Only slices, arrays, maps and strings can be indexed, each with its own index type. Several values in brackets are only valid as type arguments on a generic call.
codes.fix: Index a collection with the right index type.

codes.name: InvalidFunctionCall
codes.title: Invalid call
codes.summary: A value that is not a function is called, or a function is called with the wrong number of arguments.
codes.detail: The expression before the parentheses is not a function or method, or the call passes more or fewer arguments than it declares.
codes.fix: Call a function, with the arguments it declares.

codes.name: LogicalOperatorError
codes.title: Logical operator on non-booleans
codes.summary: An operand of &&, || or ! is not a boolean, or the operands of || are incompatible.
codes.detail: Piko does not treat non-boolean values as true or false implicitly.
codes.fix: Compare explicitly, or use the ~ operator for truthiness, such as ~value && ~other.

example.message: Invalid operation: cannot strictly compare type 'app.Level' to 'string'

codes.name: ComparisonError
codes.title: Invalid comparison
codes.summary: The two sides of a comparison cannot be compared.
codes.detail: Ordering operators (<, >, <=, >=) need ordered types of the same kind. Equality is checked strictly: a named type and a plain literal of its underlying type, such as a named string type and a string, cannot be compared directly.
codes.fix: Convert one side so both have the same type, or compare a field that has a comparable type.

codes.name: ArithmeticError
codes.title: Invalid arithmetic
codes.summary: An arithmetic operator is used with types it is not defined for.
codes.detail: Both operands of +, -, *, / and % must be compatible numbers, and unary - needs a number. Money only adds and subtracts Money, multiplies and divides by plain numbers, and has no %.
codes.fix: Convert the operands to compatible types, or use the Money methods.

codes.name: CoalesceError
codes.title: ?? operands do not match
codes.summary: The two sides of ?? have incompatible types.
codes.detail: a ?? b gives b when a is nil, so b should have a's type.
codes.fix: Give the fallback the same type as the value it replaces.

codes.name: StringConcatError
codes.title: String concatenation
codes.summary: A string concatenation involves a value that cannot be turned into a string.
codes.detail: This code is not currently reported: such concatenations are reported as invalid arithmetic (T142). The number stays assigned so it is never reused.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix.

codes.name: CoercionError
codes.title: Conversion failed
codes.summary: A value could not be converted to the type it is needed as.
codes.detail: It is an error when a conversion function has the wrong number of arguments or cannot convert the type. It is a warning when a static prop value cannot be converted to the prop's type, in which case the value is ignored.
codes.fix: Pass a value that can be converted, or change the prop's type.

codes.name: FormatDirectiveError
codes.title: Formatting function misused
codes.summary: F or LF is called incorrectly, or with a value it may not format.
codes.detail: It is an error when F or LF does not get exactly one argument. It is a warning when the argument is not a number (int, float, Decimal, BigInt or Money), a time (time.Time or DateTime) or a string.
codes.fix: Pass one value of a supported type.

codes.name: ActionError
codes.title: Action error
codes.summary: An action could not be discovered, or a template calls it incorrectly.
codes.detail: It is an error when the actions directory cannot be read or parsed, or an action has no Call method. It is a warning when a template calls an action that does not exist, or passes a field its input does not have, misses a required field, or passes the wrong type.
codes.fix: Fix the action in the actions directory, or the call in the template.

codes.name: GraphBuildError
codes.title: Entry point not found
codes.summary: An entry point of the component dependency graph could not be resolved.
codes.detail: The build starts from the project's pages and other entry points. One of them could not be found.
codes.fix: Check the path in the message, and the project's configuration.

codes.name: ClientScriptError
codes.title: Client script problem
codes.summary: A client script cannot be parsed, an event handler is missing from it, or an imported partial is never used.
codes.detail: It is an error when a client script block cannot be parsed, or when a p-on handler names a function the client script does not export. It is a warning when a partial is imported but neither rendered nor used in reloadPartial or reloadGroup.
codes.fix: Fix the script's syntax, export the handler from the client script, or remove the unused import.

codes.name: PartialCSSError
codes.title: Partial CSS error
codes.summary: A partial's CSS could not be processed when the partial was expanded.
codes.detail: When a partial is expanded into its parent, its styles are processed with the parent's. The message names the partial and the cause.
codes.fix: Fix the CSS in the named partial.

codes.name: ComputedPropertyError
codes.title: Computed property not supported
codes.summary: Member access with [...] is used where it is not supported.
codes.detail: Templates cannot access a package's members, or a variable's fields, by a computed name in brackets.
codes.fix: Use dot access, such as value.Field, or index a map instead.

codes.name: SuggestedPropName
codes.title: Suggested prop name
codes.summary: An unknown prop name is close to one the component defines.
codes.detail: This code is not currently reported: suggestions appear in the unknown prop message (T126) instead. The number stays assigned so it is never reused.
codes.fix: Nothing to fix.

codes.name: CollectionProviderNotFound
codes.title: Collection provider not registered
codes.summary: A p-collection names a provider that is not registered.
codes.detail: Pages that use the provider will not be available until it is registered.
codes.fix: Register the provider as the message describes, or fix its name.

codes.name: SitemapMarkerIgnored
codes.title: sitemap marker ignored
codes.summary: The sitemap marker is on a tag that cannot add an image to the sitemap.
codes.detail: The build-only sitemap marker is honoured only on <piko:img> and <piko:picture>.
codes.fix: Move the marker to a <piko:img> or <piko:picture>, or remove it.

example.message: p-collection-source "docs" does not match the name of any import in the Go script block; import the content module under that name

codes.name: CollectionSourceNotFound
codes.title: Collection source not imported
codes.summary: A p-collection-source alias matches no import in the Go script block.
codes.detail: p-collection-source names the import alias of the module that holds the content. Piko does not fall back to the page's local content.
codes.fix: Import the content module under that alias, or correct the alias.

codes.name: RenderError
codes.title: Render returned an error
codes.summary: A page or component's Render function returned an error.
codes.detail: The error is recorded and logged with the page's other render diagnostics, and the request is answered with an error page.
codes.fix: Handle the cause in Render, or return a piko error with a safe message for the visitor.

codes.name: PartialRenderError
codes.title: Partial Render returned an error
codes.summary: A partial's Render function returned an error.
codes.detail: The partial's error is recorded with the page's render diagnostics and logged.
codes.fix: Handle the cause in the partial's Render function.

codes.name: NilPropertyAccess
codes.title: Field read through nil
codes.summary: A template read a field through a pointer that was nil.
codes.detail: Templates guard field access through pointers that may be nil. Instead of panicking, the expression gives the field's zero value and this warning is recorded. The build reports the risk ahead of time as T101.
codes.fix: Check the value before using it, such as p-if="state.User != nil", or make sure Render sets it.

codes.name: NilIndexAccess
codes.title: Index into nil
codes.summary: A template indexed a slice or map that was nil.
codes.detail: Instead of panicking, the expression gives the zero value and this warning is recorded.
codes.fix: Make sure the slice or map is set before it is indexed, or check it first.

codes.name: IndexOutOfBounds
codes.title: Index out of range
codes.summary: A template indexed a slice outside its length.
codes.detail: Instead of panicking, the expression gives the zero value and this warning is recorded.
codes.fix: Check the length first, such as p-if="len(state.Items) > 2", or loop over the slice with p-for.

codes.name: EmptyElementTag
codes.title: <piko:element> has no tag
codes.summary: A <piko:element :is> expression resolved to an empty tag name.
codes.detail: The element cannot be rendered without a tag, so it is skipped.
codes.fix: Make sure the is expression always gives a tag name.

codes.name: RejectedElementTag
codes.title: <piko:element> tag not allowed
codes.summary: A <piko:element :is> expression resolved to a reserved tag.
codes.detail: <piko:element> cannot render piko:partial, piko:slot or piko:element, so the element is skipped.
codes.fix: Use a plain HTML tag name, or use <piko:partial> for partials.
